meaning: Start doing a new kind of work as well.
japanese: 新しい分野にも、手を広げる。
cue: A company added a different line of business.
reply: The bakery branched into catering last year.
replyJapanese: あのパン屋は昨年、仕出しにも手を広げました。
transferReply: She branched into teaching after ten years.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は10年後に、教える仕事にも広げました。
nuance: Inseparable. The longer branch out into is equally common and slightly more emphatic.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できない。長い形の branch out into も同じくらい使い、やや強調的。
contrast: Branch into adds a new area; move into can mean leaving the old one behind.
contrastJapanese: branch into は新分野を加える。move into は元の分野を離れる含みにもなる。

meaning: Walk quickly past someone, touching them lightly.
japanese: 軽く触れながら、足早に通り過ぎる。
cue: Describe a crowded corridor.
reply: Someone brushed past me without a word.
replyJapanese: 誰かが何も言わずに、私の横をかすめて行きました。
transferReply: He brushed past the reporters at the door.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼は出口で、記者たちの横をすり抜けました。
nuance: Inseparable. The touch is slight and usually accidental, though it can seem rude.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できない。触れ方はごく軽く、たいてい偶然だが、無礼に見えることもある。
contrast: Brush past touches lightly in passing; push past forces a way through.
contrastJapanese: brush past は軽く触れて通る。push past は押しのけて通る。

meaning: Sell an investment to take the money.
japanese: 換金して、利益を確定する。
cue: An owner sold their share of a business.
reply: He cashed out just before the merger.
replyJapanese: 彼は合併の直前に、持ち分を現金化しました。
transferReply: They cashed out half and kept the rest.
transferReplyJapanese: 半分を現金化して、残りは持ち続けました。
nuance: Usually intransitive; of introduces the investment. Cash in is the British equivalent.
nuanceJapanese: ふつう自動詞で、対象は of で示す。イギリス英語では cash in を使う。
contrast: Cash out sells to take the money; sell up means selling everything and leaving.
contrastJapanese: cash out は換金する。sell up はすべて売って退くこと。

meaning: Show someone evidence they cannot avoid.
japanese: 言い逃れできない事実を、突きつける。
cue: A discrepancy had to be raised directly.
reply: We confronted him with the figures.
replyJapanese: 私たちは彼に、その数字を突きつけました。
transferReply: She was confronted with the truth at last.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女はついに、真実を突きつけられました。
nuance: The person goes between confront and with. Often passive: be confronted with.
nuanceJapanese: 相手は confront と with のあいだに置く。be confronted with の受け身も多い。
contrast: Confront with presents evidence; accuse of states the charge itself.
contrastJapanese: confront with は証拠を突きつける。accuse of は罪状そのものを述べる。

meaning: Imagine something you would love to have.
japanese: いつか、と思い描く。
cue: Someone describes a long-held wish.
reply: I've dreamt about a house by the sea.
replyJapanese: 海辺の家を、ずっと思い描いてきました。
transferReply: She dreamt about her old school again.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女はまた、昔の学校の夢を見ました。
nuance: Inseparable. Dream is irregular in British English: dreamt. Dream of is close in meaning.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できない。イギリス英語では過去形 dreamt。dream of もほぼ同義。
contrast: Dream about is a wish or a sleeping dream; long for is present, felt desire.
contrastJapanese: dream about は願望や睡眠中の夢。long for は今感じている切望。

meaning: Give all your attention to one detail.
japanese: ひとつの点に、食いつく。
cue: A reader focused on one small error.
reply: Reviewers fastened on the missing date.
replyJapanese: 評者は、日付の抜けに食いつきました。
transferReply: He fastened on the one weak answer.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼は、弱い回答ひとつに食いつきました。
nuance: Inseparable; upon is the formal variant. It implies the detail is seized and not let go.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できない。upon は改まった形。一点をつかんで離さない含みがある。
contrast: Fasten on seizes one detail; dwell on keeps returning to it at length.
contrastJapanese: fasten on は一点に食いつく。dwell on は長々と繰り返し戻ること。

meaning: Praise someone excessively to gain favour.
japanese: 取り入るために、大げさに持ち上げる。
cue: A colleague flatters a senior manager.
reply: He fawns on anyone above him.
replyJapanese: 彼は上の立場の人には、誰にでも媚びます。
transferReply: The staff fawned on the visitors all evening.
transferReplyJapanese: 店員は一晩中、客に媚びていました。
nuance: Inseparable; on and over are both used. Always disapproving.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できず、on も over も使う。つねに否定的。
contrast: Fawn on is excessive flattery; look up to is sincere admiration.
contrastJapanese: fawn on は度を越したへつらい。look up to は素直な尊敬。

meaning: Expect something when making a plan.
japanese: 見込んで、計算に入れる。
cue: You are estimating how long a task takes.
reply: Figure on two hours for the drive.
replyJapanese: 運転には2時間を見込んでおいてください。
transferReply: We hadn't figured on the extra fee.
transferReplyJapanese: 追加料金は、見込んでいませんでした。
nuance: Inseparable, informal and mostly American. Often followed by a noun or an -ing form.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できないくだけた表現で、主にアメリカ英語。名詞や -ing 形を続ける。
contrast: Figure on builds an expectation into a plan; bank on relies on it heavily.
contrastJapanese: figure on は計画に織り込む。bank on は強く当てにする。

meaning: Disapprove of something mildly but clearly.
japanese: よしとせず、眉をひそめる。
cue: A workplace dislikes a common habit.
reply: They frown on phones in meetings.
replyJapanese: 会議での電話は、よく思われていません。
transferReply: Arriving early is frowned on there.
transferReplyJapanese: あそこでは、早く着くのは好まれません。
nuance: Inseparable; upon is the formal variant. Very often passive: it is frowned on.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できない。upon は改まった形。it is frowned on の受け身が非常に多い。
contrast: Frown on is mild disapproval; take a dim view of is stronger and more formal.
contrastJapanese: frown on は軽い不興。take a dim view of はより強く改まった言い方。

meaning: Contact someone about a matter.
japanese: 用件のために、連絡を取る。
cue: A supplier needs chasing.
reply: I'll get onto the printer this morning.
replyJapanese: 午前中に、印刷所に連絡します。
transferReply: She got onto the council about the noise.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は騒音の件で、自治体に連絡しました。
nuance: Inseparable; about introduces the matter. British and informal. Get is irregular: got.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できず、用件は about で示す。くだけたイギリス英語。get は不規則変化で got。
contrast: Get onto contacts someone about a matter; get through to means finally reaching them.
contrastJapanese: get onto は用件で連絡する。get through to はやっと連絡がつくこと。

meaning: Take great and open pleasure in something.
japanese: 誇らしげに、大いに楽しむ。
cue: Someone enjoys their reputation openly.
reply: He glories in being the awkward one.
replyJapanese: 彼は、扱いにくい存在であることを誇っています。
transferReply: They gloried in the quiet of the valley.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼らは谷の静けさを、心ゆくまで味わいました。
nuance: Inseparable and literary. It can be admiring or critical, depending on what is enjoyed.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できない文語的な表現。何を楽しむかで、賞賛にも批判にもなる。
contrast: Glory in is open enjoyment; revel in stresses indulging without restraint.
contrastJapanese: glory in は誇らしげに楽しむ。revel in は抑えずに浸ることを強調する。

meaning: Change to a different side or system.
japanese: 別の側や方式に、乗り換える。
cue: A team adopted a rival product.
reply: Half the office went over to the new tool.
replyJapanese: 職場の半分が、新しいツールに移りました。
transferReply: Two members went over to the other party.
transferReplyJapanese: 2名が、別の党へ移りました。
nuance: Inseparable. Go is irregular: went, gone. It implies leaving the previous side behind.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できない。go は不規則変化で went、gone。前の側を離れる含みがある。
contrast: Go over to changes sides; switch over changes system without taking sides.
contrastJapanese: go over to は陣営を変える。switch over は立場と無関係に方式を変える。

meaning: Keep talking about the same thing tediously.
japanese: 同じ話を、くどくど繰り返す。
cue: Someone repeats a complaint constantly.
reply: He harps on about the parking every week.
replyJapanese: 彼は毎週、駐車場の話をくどくど繰り返します。
transferReply: I won't harp on about it any longer.
transferReplyJapanese: これ以上、くどくど言うのはやめます。
nuance: Inseparable; British often adds about. Always critical of the repetition.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できず、イギリス英語では about を付けることが多い。繰り返しへの批判をつねに含む。
contrast: Harp on about is tedious repetition; go on about is a milder everyday version.
contrastJapanese: harp on about はくどい繰り返し。go on about はもう少し軽い日常表現。

meaning: Move directly towards a target.
japanese: 狙いを定めて、まっすぐ迫る。
cue: An investigation narrowed to one cause.
reply: They homed in on the faulty batch.
replyJapanese: 彼らは、不良ロットに的を絞りました。
transferReply: She homes in on the key sentence at once.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は即座に、肝心な一文に的を絞ります。
nuance: Intransitive; on introduces the target. The spelling is home, not hone.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞で、対象は on で示す。綴りは hone ではなく home。
contrast: Home in on narrows to a target; zero in on is a close American alternative.
contrastJapanese: home in on は的を絞る。zero in on はアメリカ英語のほぼ同義語。

meaning: Want something very strongly.
japanese: 強く、渇望する。
cue: A team wants recognition badly.
reply: They hunger for a win after that season.
replyJapanese: あのシーズンのあと、彼らは勝利に飢えています。
transferReply: She hungers for new ideas.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は新しい発想を、強く求めています。
nuance: Inseparable and literary. Hunger after is an older variant. Rarely used in casual speech.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できない文語的な表現。hunger after は古い変種。日常会話ではあまり使わない。
contrast: Hunger for is strong, almost physical want; wish for is a lighter hope.
contrastJapanese: hunger for は身体的なほど強い渇望。wish for はもっと軽い願い。

meaning: Ask someone to come with you.
japanese: 一緒に来るよう、誘う。
cue: You are adding someone to an outing.
reply: Shall we invite Marta along?
replyJapanese: マルタも誘いましょうか。
transferReply: They invited the new starter along.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼らは新入りの人も、誘いました。
nuance: Separable: invite her along. The along means joining something already planned.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：invite her along。along は既定の予定に加わる意味。
contrast: Invite along adds someone to an existing plan; invite over asks them to your home.
contrastJapanese: invite along は既存の予定に誘う。invite over は自宅に招く。

meaning: Poke or point at something sharply.
japanese: 鋭く、突く。指し示す。
cue: Describe an emphatic speaker.
reply: He jabbed at the chart as he spoke.
replyJapanese: 彼は話しながら、図を指で突いていました。
transferReply: She jabbed at the lift button twice.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女はエレベーターのボタンを、2度強く押しました。
nuance: Inseparable. Jab doubles the b: jabbed. It suggests a short, forceful movement.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できない。jab は b を重ねて jabbed。短く力のこもった動きを表す。
contrast: Jab at is a sharp poke; point at simply indicates without contact.
contrastJapanese: jab at は鋭く突くこと。point at は触れずに示すだけ。

meaning: Destroy something completely.
japanese: 完全に、絶やす。
cue: A change ended a long-standing practice.
reply: The new rule killed off the old custom.
replyJapanese: 新しい規則が、その古い慣習を絶やしました。
transferReply: She killed off the main character in book three.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は3巻目で、主人公を退場させました。
nuance: Separable: kill it off. The off means complete destruction, leaving none.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：kill it off。off は残らず絶やすことを表す。
contrast: Kill off destroys completely; wipe out stresses the scale of the loss.
contrastJapanese: kill off は完全に絶やす。wipe out は失われた規模を強調する。

meaning: Express sadness about something at length.
japanese: 長々と、嘆き悲しむ。
cue: Someone regrets a lost opportunity.
reply: There's no use lamenting over the delay.
replyJapanese: 遅れを嘆いても、仕方ありません。
transferReply: The piece laments over a vanished trade.
transferReplyJapanese: その記事は、消えた商売を惜しんでいます。
nuance: Inseparable and formal. Lament something without over is also correct.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できない改まった表現。over を付けず lament something とも言える。
contrast: Lament over expresses sorrow; dwell upon keeps returning without emotion.
contrastJapanese: lament over は悲しみを表す。dwell upon は感情なしに繰り返し戻ること。

meaning: Set up a system so it is ready to work.
japanese: 仕組みを、整えて機能させる。
cue: A safeguard has been arranged.
reply: We put in place a second check.
replyJapanese: 二重の確認を、整えました。
transferReply: The rules were put in place last April.
transferReplyJapanese: その規則は、昨年4月に整えられました。
nuance: The object can go before in: put a check in place. Often passive in formal writing.
nuanceJapanese: 目的語は in の前に置ける：put a check in place。改まった文章では受け身が多い。
contrast: Put in place establishes a system; set up can mean arranging a single event.
contrastJapanese: put in place は仕組みを整える。set up は単発の手配にも使う。

meaning: Talk quickly for a long time about little.
japanese: とりとめもなく、しゃべり続ける。
cue: Someone talks without pausing.
reply: He rattled on for twenty minutes.
replyJapanese: 彼は20分、しゃべり続けました。
transferReply: Sorry, I'm rattling on again.
transferReplyJapanese: すみません、また話し込んでしまいました。
nuance: Intransitive; about introduces the topic. Informal and mildly critical.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞で、話題は about で示す。くだけた、やや批判的な表現。
contrast: Rattle on is fast and aimless; harp on about repeats one complaint.
contrastJapanese: rattle on は早口でとりとめがない。harp on about は同じ不満を繰り返す。

meaning: Count on something when planning.
japanese: あてにして、計算に入れる。
cue: You are budgeting for a trip.
reply: Reckon on forty pounds a day.
replyJapanese: 1日40ポンドを見込んでおいてください。
transferCue: Describe a plan that went wrong.
transferReply: We hadn't reckoned on the road closure.
transferReplyJapanese: 道路の閉鎖は、計算に入れていませんでした。
nuance: Inseparable and British. Reckon on doing is the pattern before a verb.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できないイギリス英語。動詞を続けるときは reckon on doing の形。
contrast: Reckon on is a planning assumption; count on expects someone to deliver.
contrastJapanese: reckon on は計画上の前提。count on は人が果たすことを期待する。

meaning: Extend an arrangement into the next period.
japanese: 次の期間に、そのまま繰り越す。
cue: An unused allowance continues.
reply: Unused days roll over into January.
replyJapanese: 使わなかった日数は、1月に繰り越されます。
transferReply: He rolled over and went back to sleep.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼は寝返りを打って、また眠りました。
nuance: Intransitive here; the noun is a rollover. The literal turning sense is also common.
nuanceJapanese: ここでは自動詞で、名詞は rollover。「寝返る」という文字どおりの意味もよく使う。
contrast: Roll over carries an arrangement forward; carry over moves an amount or a feeling.
contrastJapanese: roll over は取り決めを持ち越す。carry over は数量や気持ちを持ち越す。

meaning: Tell someone an idea to get their reaction.
japanese: 反応を見るために、ひとこと通しておく。
cue: You want a quick opinion before acting.
reply: Can I run the wording past you?
replyJapanese: この文言、ちょっと見てもらえますか。
transferReply: She ran the budget past her manager first.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女はまず、予算を上司に通しました。
nuance: The idea goes between run and past. Run is irregular: ran, run. Informal but common at work.
nuanceJapanese: 案は run と past のあいだに置く。run は不規則変化で ran、run。くだけているが職場でよく使う。
contrast: Run past seeks a quick reaction; run by is the American form of the same idea.
contrastJapanese: run past は素早い反応を求める。run by はアメリカ英語の同じ言い方。

meaning: Produce and release something very quickly.
japanese: 急ごしらえで、世に出す。
cue: A product appeared sooner than expected.
reply: They rushed out a fix the same evening.
replyJapanese: 彼らはその晩のうちに、修正を出しました。
transferReply: The biography was rushed out in weeks.
transferReplyJapanese: その伝記は、数週間で急いで出版されました。
nuance: Separable: rush it out. Often passive, and it can suggest the quality suffered.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：rush it out。受け身が多く、質が落ちた含みになることもある。
contrast: Rush out releases hastily; roll out describes a planned, staged release.
contrastJapanese: rush out は急いで出す。roll out は計画的に段階を踏む公開。

meaning: Look much better once cleaned and dressed.
japanese: 身なりを整えると、見違える。
cue: Someone looks unexpectedly smart.
reply: You scrub up well.
replyJapanese: ずいぶん見違えましたね。
transferReply: The old hall scrubs up nicely.
transferReplyJapanese: あの古い会館も、手を入れると見違えます。
nuance: Intransitive, British and informal, almost always with well or nicely. A friendly compliment.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞のくだけたイギリス英語で、ほぼつねに well や nicely を伴う。親しみのある褒め言葉。
contrast: Scrub up is about looking better when cleaned; smarten up is the act of tidying.
contrastJapanese: scrub up は整えた結果よく見えること。smarten up は整える行為そのもの。

meaning: Sell something you recently bought to someone else.
japanese: 買ったものを、さらに他へ売る。
cue: Goods were bought and resold quickly.
reply: They sold the tickets on at a profit.
replyJapanese: 彼らはその券を、利益を乗せて転売しました。
transferReply: I sold it on after a year.
transferReplyJapanese: 1年後に、それを売り渡しました。
nuance: Separable: sell it on. Sell is irregular: sold. British; American English says resell.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：sell it on。sell は不規則変化で sold。イギリス英語で、アメリカ英語では resell。
contrast: Sell on passes goods to a further buyer; sell off clears stock cheaply.
contrastJapanese: sell on は次の買い手へ売る。sell off は安く在庫を処分する。

meaning: Attack someone suddenly.
japanese: 突然、襲いかかる。
cue: Describe an incident with a dog.
reply: He was set on by two dogs.
replyJapanese: 彼は2匹の犬に襲われました。
transferReply: The speaker was set on by hecklers.
transferReplyJapanese: 話し手は、野次を飛ばす人々に責め立てられました。
nuance: Almost always passive: be set on by. Set is irregular and unchanged in all forms.
nuanceJapanese: ほぼつねに be set on by の受け身。set は不規則変化で形が変わらない。
contrast: Set on is a sudden attack; turn on means a friend becoming hostile.
contrastJapanese: set on は突然の襲撃。turn on は味方が敵意を見せること。

meaning: Test something new until it settles into working order.
japanese: 慣らし運転をして、不具合を出しきる。
cue: A new process needs a trial period.
reply: Give it a month to shake down.
replyJapanese: 落ち着くまで、1か月見てください。
transferReply: The group is still shaking down.
transferReplyJapanese: その班は、まだ慣らし中です。
nuance: Intransitive here; the noun is a shakedown, a trial run. Shake is irregular: shook, shaken.
nuanceJapanese: ここでは自動詞で、名詞 shakedown は「試運転」。shake は不規則変化で shook、shaken。
contrast: Shake down settles into working order; bed in describes the same process for a system.
contrastJapanese: shake down は動くまで落ち着くこと。制度については bed in が同じ過程を表す。

meaning: Leave, said rudely or jokingly.
japanese: 「もう行け」と、そっけなく言う。
cue: Friends are teasing each other.
reply: Oh, shove off — you know that's not true.
replyJapanese: やめてくださいよ。違うって分かっているでしょう。
transferReply: We shoved off before the rain started.
transferReplyJapanese: 雨が降り出す前に、私たちは発ちました。
nuance: Intransitive, British and informal. Rude to a stranger, but friendly between people who know each other.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞のくだけたイギリス英語。見知らぬ相手には失礼だが、親しい間では冗談になる。
contrast: Shove off dismisses or departs bluntly; push off is the same idea, slightly milder.
contrastJapanese: shove off はそっけなく追い払う・去る。push off は同じ意味でやや穏やか。

meaning: Walk away slowly and without energy.
japanese: 足を引きずるように、のろのろ去る。
cue: Describe someone leaving reluctantly.
reply: He shuffled off without looking back.
replyJapanese: 彼は振り返らず、のろのろと去りました。
transferCue: Describe the end of a queue.
transferReply: The last few shuffled off towards the exit.
transferReplyJapanese: 最後の数人が、出口へのろのろ向かいました。
nuance: Intransitive. It pictures dragging feet, and suggests low spirits or tiredness.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞。足を引きずる様子から、元気のなさや疲れを含意する。
contrast: Shuffle off leaves slowly; slope off leaves quietly to avoid notice.
contrastJapanese: shuffle off はのろのろ去る。slope off は気づかれないようそっと去る。

meaning: Make something last longer than it needs to.
japanese: 必要以上に、引き延ばす。
cue: A short item took the whole meeting.
reply: They spun out the discussion for an hour.
replyJapanese: 彼らはその議論を、1時間に引き延ばしました。
transferReply: She spun out her savings for a year.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は貯金を、1年もたせました。
nuance: Separable: spin it out. Spin is irregular: spun. Often mildly critical about time.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：spin it out。spin は不規則変化で spun。時間については、やや批判的になる。
contrast: Spin out prolongs unnecessarily; stretch out can be a sensible way to make something last.
contrastJapanese: spin out は無駄に長引かせる。stretch out は賢く長持ちさせる場合にも使う。

meaning: Settle something so it is fully sorted out.
japanese: きちんと片づけて、決着させる。
cue: Remaining details were resolved.
reply: We squared away the paperwork on Friday.
replyJapanese: 金曜に、書類を片づけました。
transferReply: Once the visa is squared away we can book.
transferReplyJapanese: ビザが片づいたら、予約できます。
nuance: Separable: square it away. Informal and mostly American. Often passive.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：square it away。くだけた主にアメリカ英語で、受け身も多い。
contrast: Square away settles something fully; tidy up only puts things in order.
contrastJapanese: square away は完全に決着させる。tidy up は整えるだけ。

meaning: Publicly oppose something.
japanese: 公然と、反対の立場を取る。
cue: A group opposed a proposal openly.
reply: They stood against the closure from the start.
replyJapanese: 彼らは最初から、閉鎖に反対の立場でした。
transferReply: She stands against any form of it.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女はどんな形であれ、それに反対です。
nuance: Inseparable. Stand is irregular: stood. It implies a public, principled position.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できない。stand は不規則変化で stood。公に、信念として反対する含みがある。
contrast: Stand against opposes openly; stand up to confronts a specific stronger party.
contrastJapanese: stand against は公に反対する。stand up to は強い相手に立ち向かう。

meaning: Fasten a seat belt, or prepare for something intense.
japanese: ベルトを締める。身構える。
cue: You are getting into a car with a child.
reply: Strap in before we set off.
replyJapanese: 出発する前に、ベルトを締めてください。
transferReply: Strap in — the next month is busy.
transferReplyJapanese: 覚悟してください。来月は忙しくなります。
nuance: Separable: strap her in. The figurative warning sense is informal and quite recent.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：strap her in。比喩の「身構えろ」はくだけた、比較的新しい用法。
contrast: Strap in fastens or braces; buckle up is the everyday alternative for seat belts.
contrastJapanese: strap in はベルトを締める・身構える。日常のベルトには buckle up をよく使う。

meaning: Carry someone forward with great force or enthusiasm.
japanese: 勢いに乗せて、押し流す。
cue: A crowd's mood carried everyone with it.
reply: We were swept along by the excitement.
replyJapanese: その熱気に、私たちも押し流されました。
transferReply: The branch was swept along by the river.
transferReplyJapanese: その枝は、川に押し流されました。
nuance: Often passive: be swept along by. Sweep is irregular: swept. Literal and figurative.
nuanceJapanese: be swept along by の受け身が多い。sweep は不規則変化で swept。文字どおりにも比喩にも使う。
contrast: Sweep along carries you with a force; get carried away is losing your own restraint.
contrastJapanese: sweep along は外の力に押し流される。get carried away は自分の抑えが利かなくなること。

meaning: Add something at the end, often as an afterthought.
japanese: 後づけで、末尾に足す。
cue: A late item was added to an agenda.
reply: They tacked a third item onto the agenda.
replyJapanese: 議題の末尾に、3つ目が後づけで足されました。
transferReply: A service fee was tacked onto the bill.
transferReplyJapanese: 請求に、サービス料が後から足されました。
nuance: Separable: tack it onto. On and onto are both used, and it often implies poor integration.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：tack it onto。on も onto も使い、取ってつけた印象を含むことが多い。
contrast: Tack onto adds as an afterthought; build into makes it part of the design.
contrastJapanese: tack onto は後づけで足す。build into は設計に組み込む。

meaning: Type or knock out a message with the fingers.
japanese: 指で、打ち込む。たたき出す。
cue: Describe writing on a phone.
reply: She tapped out a reply on the train.
replyJapanese: 彼女は電車で、返信を打ちました。
transferReply: He tapped out the beat on the table.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼は机で、リズムを刻みました。
nuance: Separable: tap it out. Tap doubles the p: tapped. It suggests light, quick finger movements.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：tap it out。tap は p を重ねて tapped。軽く素早い指の動きを表す。
contrast: Tap out is typing or drumming lightly; bash out stresses speed over care.
contrastJapanese: tap out は軽く打つこと。bash out は丁寧さより速さを強調する。

meaning: Continue steadily without problems or excitement.
japanese: 波風なく、淡々と続く。
cue: Someone asks how a project is going.
reply: It's ticking along nicely, thanks.
replyJapanese: おかげさまで、順調に進んでいます。
transferReply: The shop ticks along without much change.
transferReplyJapanese: その店は、大きな変化もなく続いています。
nuance: Intransitive, British and informal, often with nicely. From a clock ticking steadily.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞のくだけたイギリス英語で、nicely を伴うことが多い。時計が刻む様子から。
contrast: Tick along is steady and calm; plod along suggests it is dull and slow.
contrastJapanese: tick along は穏やかで順調。plod along は退屈で遅い含みがある。

meaning: Direct all your attention to one thing.
japanese: 一点に、狙いを絞る。
cue: An analysis narrowed to one factor.
reply: They zeroed in on the delivery times.
replyJapanese: 彼らは、配送時間に的を絞りました。
transferReply: She zeroed in on the missing data.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は、欠けているデータに的を絞りました。
nuance: Intransitive; on introduces the target. Mostly American; home in on is the British form.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞で、対象は on で示す。主にアメリカ英語で、イギリス英語では home in on。
contrast: Zero in on narrows to one target; focus on can hold a broader subject.
contrastJapanese: zero in on は一点に絞る。focus on はもっと広い対象も扱える。

meaning: Make success harder for someone.
japanese: 不利に、はたらく。
cue: A factor reduces someone's chances.
reply: His inexperience works against him here.
replyJapanese: ここでは、彼の経験の浅さが不利にはたらきます。
transferReply: Time is working against us now.
transferReplyJapanese: 今は、時間が味方していません。
nuance: Inseparable. The subject is the unhelpful factor, not the person it affects.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できない。主語は不利にはたらく要因で、影響を受ける人ではない。
contrast: Work against is a factor that hinders; hold against is blaming a person for something.
contrastJapanese: work against は妨げになる要因。hold against は人の落ち度を責めること。

meaning: Request help from someone.
japanese: お願いごとを、頼む。
cue: You need help from a colleague.
reply: Can I ask a favour before you go?
replyJapanese: 帰る前に、ひとつお願いしてもいいですか。
transferReply: She asked a favour of me last week.
transferReplyJapanese: 先週、彼女から頼まれごとをされました。
nuance: Favour takes a. British spelling is favour, American favor. Of introduces the person asked.
nuanceJapanese: favour には a を付ける。イギリス英語は favour、アメリカ英語は favor。相手は of で示す。

meaning: Make an obvious question arise.
japanese: 当然の疑問を、招く。
cue: An explanation leaves something unexplained.
reply: That begs the question of who pays.
replyJapanese: それでは、誰が払うのかという疑問が残ります。
transferReply: The figures beg the question of accuracy.
transferReplyJapanese: その数字は、正確さへの疑問を招きます。
nuance: Question takes the. In logic it means assuming your conclusion, but the everyday sense is now standard.
nuanceJapanese: question には the を付ける。論理学では「論点先取」だが、日常の用法が今では標準。

meaning: Escape from something that holds you.
japanese: 縛りから、抜け出す。
cue: Someone left a routine that limited them.
reply: She broke free of the same old pattern.
replyJapanese: 彼女は、同じ繰り返しから抜け出しました。
transferReply: The dog broke free and ran into the field.
transferReplyJapanese: 犬は綱を解いて、野原へ駆け出しました。
nuance: Break is irregular: broke, broken. Of or from introduces what held you.
nuanceJapanese: break は不規則変化で broke、broken。束縛は of または from で示す。

meaning: Become free from what was holding something.
japanese: 外れて、自由になる。
cue: Something came away in bad weather.
reply: The boat broke loose in the storm.
replyJapanese: 嵐で、船が係留から外れました。
transferReply: Two horses broke loose overnight.
transferReplyJapanese: 夜のうちに、馬が2頭逃げ出しました。
nuance: Break is irregular: broke, broken. Loose is an adjective here, never the verb lose.
nuanceJapanese: break は不規則変化で broke、broken。ここでの loose は形容詞で、動詞 lose ではない。

meaning: Two people or things that are completely different.
japanese: まるで似ていない、正反対の二つ。
cue: Two colleagues work in opposite ways.
reply: Those two are chalk and cheese.
replyJapanese: あの二人は、まるで正反対です。
transferReply: The two shops are chalk and cheese.
transferReplyJapanese: あの2店舗は、まるで違います。
nuance: British and fixed, with no articles. Usually about exactly two things being compared.
nuanceJapanese: 冠詞を付けないイギリス英語の固定表現。ふつう2つを比べるときに使う。

meaning: Used before a criticism you are pretending not to make.
japanese: 僭越ながら、と前置きする言い方。
cue: You want to raise a point tactfully.
reply: Far be it from me to argue, but the date is wrong.
replyJapanese: 僭越ですが、日付が違っています。
transferReply: Far be it from me to tell you your job.
transferReplyJapanese: 釈迦に説法でしょうが、ひとことだけ。
frame: Far be it from me to do something
nuance: Fixed and slightly ironic: it usually precedes exactly the remark it disclaims.
nuanceJapanese: やや皮肉を含む固定表現。否定したはずの指摘が、たいてい直後に続く。

meaning: Permanently, not to be given back.
japanese: 返さなくてよい、ずっと自分のもの。
cue: A child asks whether they can keep a gift.
reply: Yes, it's yours for keeps.
replyJapanese: ええ、ずっとあなたのものですよ。
transferReply: They've moved back for keeps this time.
transferReplyJapanese: 今度こそ、彼らは本当に戻ってきました。
nuance: Keeps is always plural and takes no article. Informal and warm.
nuanceJapanese: keeps はつねに複数形で、冠詞は付かない。くだけた、温かい表現。

meaning: Become organised and start working properly.
japanese: 態勢を立て直して、きちんとやる。
cue: A team has been disorganised.
reply: We need to get it together before Monday.
replyJapanese: 月曜までに、態勢を立て直す必要があります。
transferReply: He got it together after a difficult year.
transferReplyJapanese: つらい一年のあと、彼は立て直しました。
nuance: Fixed with it. Get is irregular: got. Informal, about organisation or emotional state.
nuanceJapanese: it を伴う固定表現。get は不規則変化で got。段取りにも心の状態にも使うくだけた言い方。

meaning: Return to the very beginning after a failure.
japanese: 振り出しに、戻る。
cue: An approach did not work at all.
reply: We had to go back to square one.
replyJapanese: 振り出しに戻るしかありませんでした。
transferReply: One mistake and you go back to square one.
transferReplyJapanese: ひとつ間違えると、振り出しに戻ります。
nuance: Square one is singular with no article before square. Go is irregular: went, gone.
nuanceJapanese: square one は単数で、square の前に冠詞は付かない。go は不規則変化で went、gone。

meaning: Be gentle, or use only a small amount.
japanese: 手加減する。控えめにする。
cue: Someone is adding a strong ingredient.
reply: Go easy on the salt.
replyJapanese: 塩は控えめにしてください。
transferReply: Go easy on him — it's his first week.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼には優しくしてください。まだ最初の週です。
nuance: On introduces the person or the ingredient. Easy is an adverb here, not easily.
nuanceJapanese: 対象は on で示す。ここでの easy は副詞で、easily とは言わない。

meaning: An advantage gained by starting earlier.
japanese: 先に始めたことによる、有利。
cue: One group began before the others.
reply: They had a head start of two weeks.
replyJapanese: 彼らには、2週間の先行がありました。
transferReply: Reading the brief gives you a head start.
transferReplyJapanese: 要項を読んでおくと、一歩先に進めます。
nuance: Countable, so it takes a. Usually with have or give. From racing.
nuanceJapanese: 可算名詞なので a を付ける。ふつう have や give と使う。競走に由来する。

meaning: Very soon, almost immediately.
japanese: すぐに。あっという間に。
cue: You are asking someone to wait briefly.
reply: I'll be with you in two shakes.
replyJapanese: すぐに伺います。
transferReply: She had it fixed in two shakes.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女はあっという間に、直してしまいました。
nuance: Shakes is always plural and the number is always two. Informal and a little old-fashioned.
nuanceJapanese: shakes はつねに複数形で、数字も two で固定。くだけた、やや古風な表現。

meaning: Said when you meet someone unexpectedly connected to you.
japanese: 世間は狭い、という驚きの言葉。
cue: A stranger turns out to know your friend.
reply: You know Ben too? It's a small world.
replyJapanese: ベンをご存じなのですか。世間は狭いですね。
transferReply: We grew up on the same street — it's a small world.
transferReplyJapanese: 同じ通りで育ったなんて、世間は狭いものです。
nuance: Fixed and always in this form. It marks a coincidence, not an opinion about the world.
nuanceJapanese: この形で固定。世界観ではなく、偶然への驚きを表す。

meaning: React to someone with sudden anger.
japanese: いきなり、きつく食ってかかる。
cue: A mild question got an angry answer.
reply: He jumped down my throat for asking.
replyJapanese: 尋ねただけで、彼にきつく言い返されました。
transferReply: There's no need to jump down my throat.
transferReplyJapanese: そんなに食ってかからなくてもいいでしょう。
nuance: The possessive follows the person spoken to, and throat stays singular.
nuanceJapanese: 所有格は相手に合わせ、throat は単数のまま。

meaning: Earn just enough to survive.
japanese: やっと、食べていけるだけ稼ぐ。
cue: Describe a very low income.
reply: The work barely keeps body and soul together.
replyJapanese: その仕事では、やっと食べていける程度です。
transferReply: Two jobs kept body and soul together that winter.
transferReplyJapanese: あの冬は、仕事を2つ掛け持ちして食いつなぎました。
nuance: Fixed with no articles. Keep is irregular: kept. It stresses bare survival.
nuanceJapanese: 冠詞を付けない固定表現。keep は不規則変化で kept。ぎりぎりの生活を強調する。

meaning: An indirect result caused by an earlier change.
japanese: あとから連鎖して出る、間接的な影響。
cue: One delay caused several others.
reply: The strike had a knock-on effect on deliveries.
replyJapanese: ストライキは、配送に連鎖的な影響を与えました。
transferReply: There was a knock-on effect for smaller firms.
transferReplyJapanese: 小さな会社にも、連鎖的な影響が及びました。
frame: Have a knock-on effect on something
nuance: Hyphenated before effect, and countable, so it takes a. British; American English says ripple effect.
nuanceJapanese: effect の前ではハイフンを付け、可算なので a を伴う。イギリス英語で、アメリカ英語では ripple effect。

meaning: The final option when nothing else works.
japanese: ほかに手がないときの、最後の手段。
cue: An unattractive option remains.
reply: Borrowing is a last resort.
replyJapanese: 借りるのは、最後の手段です。
transferReply: As a last resort, we cancelled the trip.
transferReplyJapanese: 最後の手段として、旅行を取りやめました。
nuance: Usually with a in as a last resort, or with the when the option is already known.
nuanceJapanese: as a last resort では a を使い、特定の手段を指すときは the を使う。

meaning: Argue strongly with someone who will not give way.
japanese: 互いに譲らず、真っ向から争う。
cue: Two departments disagreed firmly.
reply: They locked horns over the budget again.
replyJapanese: 彼らはまた、予算をめぐって真っ向からぶつかりました。
transferReply: Those two lock horns at every meeting.
transferReplyJapanese: あの二人は、会議のたびにぶつかります。
nuance: Horns is always plural with no article. With introduces the opponent, over the subject.
nuanceJapanese: horns はつねに複数形で、冠詞は付かない。相手は with、争点は over で示す。

meaning: Pretend that something is true.
japanese: そうだということにして、ふりをする。
cue: Describe children playing.
reply: They make believe the box is a boat.
replyJapanese: 子どもたちは、箱を船に見立てて遊びます。
transferReply: Let's not make believe the problem has gone.
transferReplyJapanese: 問題が消えたふりをするのは、やめましょう。
nuance: Make is irregular: made. As a noun it is written make-believe, meaning pretence.
nuanceJapanese: make は不規則変化で made。名詞では make-believe と書き、「ごっこ・作りごと」の意味。

meaning: Finish something quickly and easily.
japanese: あっさり、片づけてしまう。
cue: A task took far less time than expected.
reply: She made short work of the backlog.
replyJapanese: 彼女は、たまった仕事をあっさり片づけました。
transferReply: They made short work of the sandwiches.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼らは、サンドイッチをあっという間に平らげました。
nuance: Fixed with no article before short work. Make is irregular: made.
nuanceJapanese: short work の前に冠詞を付けない固定表現。make は不規則変化で made。

meaning: A birthday greeting wishing more such days.
japanese: よいお誕生日を、と祝う言葉。
cue: You are greeting someone on their birthday.
reply: Many happy returns of the day.
replyJapanese: お誕生日おめでとうございます。
transferReply: Many happy returns from all of us.
transferReplyJapanese: 私たち一同より、お誕生日のお祝いを申し上げます。
nuance: British, fixed and always plural. The longer form adds of the day. Only for birthdays.
nuanceJapanese: つねに複数形のイギリス英語の固定表現。長い形は of the day を付ける。誕生日にのみ使う。

meaning: Wait without making progress.
japanese: 進まないまま、足踏みする。
cue: A team is waiting for a decision.
reply: We're marking time until the funding is confirmed.
replyJapanese: 資金が確定するまで、足踏みしています。
transferCue: Describe a career that stopped moving.
transferReply: He marked time in that role for years.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼はその役職で、何年も足踏みしていました。
nuance: Time takes no article. From marching on the spot, so it implies effort without movement.
nuanceJapanese: time に冠詞は付かない。その場での足踏み行進から、進まない努力を表す。

meaning: Die, said gently or humorously.
japanese: 亡くなることを、やわらかく言う言い方。
cue: Describe an old machine breaking down for good.
reply: That printer has finally met its maker.
replyJapanese: あのプリンターも、ついに天寿を全うしました。
transferReply: He went to meet his maker last winter.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼は昨冬、旅立ちました。
nuance: The possessive follows the subject. Meet is irregular: met. A euphemism, so use it with care.
nuanceJapanese: 所有格は主語に合わせる。meet は不規則変化で met。婉曲表現なので、使う場面に注意。

meaning: Be careful to behave politely.
japanese: 言葉づかいや振る舞いに、気をつける。
cue: Someone is going somewhere formal.
reply: Mind your p's and q's at the interview.
replyJapanese: 面接では、言葉づかいに気をつけてください。
transferReply: You'll need to mind your p's and q's there.
transferReplyJapanese: あそこでは、振る舞いに気をつける必要があります。
nuance: British, fixed, and both letters are written with an apostrophe and s. Usually advice before an event.
nuanceJapanese: イギリス英語の固定表現で、どちらの文字にもアポストロフィと s を付ける。ふつう行事の前の助言。

meaning: Money earned for very little effort.
japanese: ほとんど手間なく、得られる収入。
cue: A task pays well and takes minutes.
reply: Two hundred for an hour? Money for old rope.
replyJapanese: 1時間で200ですか。おいしい話ですね。
transferReply: Marking the forms was money for old rope.
transferReplyJapanese: 書類に印を付けるだけで、楽な稼ぎでした。
nuance: British and informal, with no articles. Slightly envious or dismissive in tone.
nuanceJapanese: 冠詞を付けないくだけたイギリス英語。うらやみや軽い皮肉の響きがある。

phrase: nail your colours to the mast
meaning: State your position publicly and commit to it.
japanese: 立場を明らかにして、退かない。
cue: Someone declares where they stand.
reply: She nailed her colours to the mast early.
replyJapanese: 彼女は早い段階で、立場をはっきりさせました。
transferReply: It's time to nail your colours to the mast.
transferReplyJapanese: そろそろ、立場を明らかにすべきときです。
slug: nail your colours to the mast
aliases: nail her colours to the mast
frame: Nail your colours to the mast
nuance: British; American English writes colors. From a ship that cannot lower its flag to surrender.
nuanceJapanese: イギリス英語で、アメリカ英語では colors と綴る。降伏の旗を下ろせない船に由来する。

meaning: Close enough to be treated as correct.
japanese: 実質、それで差し支えない程度に近い。
cue: A rough measurement is acceptable.
reply: Two metres is near enough.
replyJapanese: 2メートルで、ほぼ問題ありません。
transferReply: Near enough fifty people came.
transferReplyJapanese: およそ50人が来ました。
nuance: British and informal. It can follow the figure or come before it as an approximation.
nuanceJapanese: くだけたイギリス英語。数字のあとにも、前に置いて概数を示すこともできる。

meaning: On your own initiative, without being asked.
japanese: 頼まれず、自分の判断で。
cue: Someone improved a process unprompted.
reply: He rewrote the guide off his own bat.
replyJapanese: 彼は頼まれもせず、手引きを書き直しました。
transferReply: I did it off my own bat.
transferReplyJapanese: 自分の判断で、やりました。
frame: Do something off your own bat
nuance: British, from cricket. The possessive follows the subject, and it is bat, not back.
nuanceJapanese: クリケット由来のイギリス英語。所有格は主語に合わせ、back ではなく bat。

meaning: A joke or story told too many times.
japanese: 何度も聞かされた、古い話。
cue: Someone repeats a familiar joke.
reply: Not that old chestnut again.
replyJapanese: また、その古い話ですか。
transferReply: It's the same old chestnut every year.
transferReplyJapanese: 毎年、同じ使い古された話です。
nuance: Countable, usually with that or the same old. Affectionate or weary, rarely harsh.
nuanceJapanese: 可算名詞で、ふつう that や the same old を伴う。厳しい非難ではなく、親しみやうんざりを表す。

meaning: In a comfortable financial position.
japanese: 金銭的に、何不自由ない状態。
cue: Someone's finances improved greatly.
reply: After the sale they were on easy street.
replyJapanese: 売却のあと、彼らは何不自由なくなりました。
transferReply: We're comfortable, but hardly on easy street.
transferReplyJapanese: 暮らしは安定していますが、裕福とは言えません。
nuance: American and informal. Street takes no article here, and the phrase is always with on.
nuanceJapanese: くだけたアメリカ英語。ここでの street に冠詞は付かず、つねに on と使う。

meaning: Unprepared when something happens.
japanese: 不意を突かれて、準備のないまま。
cue: A question arrived without warning.
reply: That question caught me on the hop.
replyJapanese: あの質問には、不意を突かれました。
transferReply: The inspection caught them on the hop.
transferReplyJapanese: 検査に、彼らは不意を突かれました。
nuance: British and informal, almost always with catch. Hop takes the.
nuanceJapanese: ほぼつねに catch と使うくだけたイギリス英語。hop には the を付ける。

meaning: Easy to decide because the facts are clear.
japanese: 事実が明白で、判断に迷わない。
cue: A decision needs no debate.
reply: It's an open and shut case.
replyJapanese: 議論の余地のない案件です。
transferReply: The insurance claim was open and shut.
transferReplyJapanese: その保険請求は、明白でした。
nuance: Usually before case, and often hyphenated as open-and-shut. It claims there is no real doubt.
nuanceJapanese: ふつう case の前に置き、open-and-shut とハイフンで綴ることも多い。疑いの余地がないことを主張する。

meaning: Extremely thin, or barely convincing.
japanese: 紙のように薄い。説得力に乏しい。
cue: An explanation does not convince you.
reply: The excuse was paper thin.
replyJapanese: その言い訳は、いかにも苦しいものでした。
transferReply: The walls here are paper thin.
transferReplyJapanese: ここの壁は、紙のように薄いです。
nuance: Often hyphenated before a noun: a paper-thin excuse. Literal for thickness, figurative for arguments.
nuanceJapanese: 名詞の前ではハイフンを付けることが多い。厚みにも、議論の弱さにも使う。

meaning: A free choice of items from a range.
japanese: 好きなものを、自由に選び取ること。
cue: A course lets students choose modules.
reply: The programme is pick and mix.
replyJapanese: その課程は、自由に選べる方式です。
transferReply: Treat the list as pick and mix.
transferReplyJapanese: その一覧は、好きに選んでよいものと考えてください。
nuance: British, from sweet shops where you fill your own bag. Used as an adjective without articles.
nuanceJapanese: 自分で袋に詰める菓子売り場に由来するイギリス英語。冠詞なしで形容詞のように使う。

meaning: Do exactly what an opponent wanted.
japanese: 相手の思うつぼに、はまる。
cue: A reaction helped the other side.
reply: Arguing publicly plays into their hands.
replyJapanese: 公の場で言い合えば、相手の思うつぼです。
transferReply: Resigning now would play into his hands.
transferReplyJapanese: 今辞めれば、彼の思うつぼになります。
nuance: Hands is always plural, and the possessive names the person who benefits.
nuanceJapanese: hands はつねに複数形で、所有格は得をする側を指す。

meaning: Something is judged by how it actually performs.
japanese: 実際にやってみて、初めて分かる。
cue: A plan looks good but is untested.
reply: The proof of the pudding is in the eating.
replyJapanese: 実際にやってみないと、分かりません。
transferCue: Reserve judgement on a new product.
transferReply: It sounds good, but proof of the pudding.
transferReplyJapanese: よさそうですが、結果を見てからですね。
frame: The proof of the pudding is in the eating
nuance: Proof takes the in the full saying. The shortened form is common in speech.
nuanceJapanese: 完全な形では proof に the を付ける。会話では短い形もよく使う。

meaning: Said rudely or jokingly to tell someone to be quiet.
japanese: 「静かにして」と、ぶっきらぼうに言う。
cue: Friends are teasing each other loudly.
reply: Put a sock in it, you two.
replyJapanese: 二人とも、少し静かにしてください。
transferReply: Someone told him to put a sock in it.
transferReplyJapanese: 誰かが彼に、黙るように言いました。
nuance: British, informal and fixed with a and it. Rude to a stranger, but playful between friends.
nuanceJapanese: a と it を伴うくだけたイギリス英語の固定表現。見知らぬ相手には失礼だが、友人同士では冗談。

meaning: Force someone to answer or decide immediately.
japanese: その場で答えを迫って、困らせる。
cue: A question came without warning in a meeting.
reply: I was put on the spot in front of everyone.
replyJapanese: みんなの前で、答えを迫られました。
transferReply: Nobody likes being put on the spot.
transferReplyJapanese: その場で答えを迫られるのは、誰でも嫌なものです。
nuance: Usually passive because the focus is on the person under pressure. Spot takes the.
nuanceJapanese: 迫られる側に焦点があるため、ふつう受け身。spot には the を付ける。

meaning: A polite refusal now with the intention of accepting later.
japanese: 今回は見送り、またの機会に、という返事。
cue: You cannot accept an invitation today.
reply: Can I take a rain check on dinner?
replyJapanese: 夕食は、またの機会にしてもよいですか。
transferReply: She took a rain check on the trip.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女はその旅行を、次の機会にしました。
frame: Take a rain check on something
nuance: American, from a ticket for a rained-off game. Almost always with take a.
nuanceJapanese: 雨天中止の試合の振替券に由来するアメリカ英語。ほぼつねに take a と使う。

meaning: Be far better than someone at something.
japanese: 相手をはるかに、上回る。
cue: One person is much faster than the rest.
reply: She runs circles around the rest of us.
replyJapanese: 彼女は、私たちをはるかに上回っています。
transferReply: The younger team ran circles around them.
transferReplyJapanese: 若いチームが、相手を圧倒しました。
nuance: Run is irregular: ran, run. British often says run rings around instead.
nuanceJapanese: run は不規則変化で ran、run。イギリス英語では run rings around と言うことが多い。

meaning: Face a line of people who criticise or attack you.
japanese: 非難の列を、くぐり抜ける。
cue: Someone walked past hostile crowds.
reply: He ran the gauntlet of photographers.
replyJapanese: 彼は、カメラマンの列をくぐり抜けました。
transferReply: Every draft runs the gauntlet of the committee.
transferReplyJapanese: 草案はどれも、委員会の厳しい審査をくぐります。
nuance: Gauntlet takes the. Run is irregular: ran, run. Of introduces who does the criticising.
nuanceJapanese: gauntlet には the を付ける。run は不規則変化で ran、run。批判する側は of で示す。

meaning: Sell very quickly and in large numbers.
japanese: 飛ぶように、売れる。
cue: A product sold out immediately.
reply: The tickets sold like hotcakes.
replyJapanese: その券は、飛ぶように売れました。
transferReply: It sells like hotcakes every December.
transferReplyJapanese: それは毎年12月に、飛ぶように売れます。
nuance: Sell is irregular: sold. Hotcakes is always plural. Mostly American, but widely understood.
nuanceJapanese: sell は不規則変化で sold。hotcakes はつねに複数形。主にアメリカ英語だが広く通じる。

meaning: Improve your behaviour or leave.
japanese: 態度を改めるか、出ていくかだ。
cue: A manager gives a final warning.
reply: The message was shape up or ship out.
replyJapanese: 改めるか去るか、という通告でした。
transferReply: It's shape up or ship out there.
transferReplyJapanese: あそこは、改めるか去るかの世界です。
nuance: American, fixed and blunt. It works as a quoted ultimatum rather than a gentle request.
nuanceJapanese: アメリカ英語の、そっけない固定表現。穏やかな依頼ではなく、最後通告として使う。

meaning: Cry, or feel sorrow about something.
japanese: 涙を流す。悲しむ。
cue: A closure was not widely mourned.
reply: Few people shed tears when it closed.
replyJapanese: 閉店を惜しんだ人は、ほとんどいませんでした。
transferReply: Nobody shed tears until the last scene.
transferReplyJapanese: 最後の場面まで、誰も涙を見せませんでした。
nuance: Tears is always plural. Shed is irregular and unchanged in all forms.
nuanceJapanese: tears はつねに複数形。shed は不規則変化で形が変わらない。

meaning: Avoid choosing between two sides.
japanese: どちらにも付かず、態度を決めない。
cue: Someone refuses to take a position.
reply: He's sitting on the fence as usual.
replyJapanese: 彼はいつもどおり、態度を決めずにいます。
transferReply: You can't sit on the fence forever.
transferReplyJapanese: いつまでも、どっちつかずではいられません。
nuance: Fence takes the. Sit is irregular: sat. Usually mildly critical.
nuanceJapanese: fence には the を付ける。sit は不規則変化で sat。ふつう軽い批判を含む。

meaning: A very short distance away.
japanese: 目と鼻の先の、近さ。
cue: Describe how close a station is.
reply: The flat is within spitting distance of the station.
replyJapanese: その部屋は、駅から目と鼻の先です。
transferReply: They finished within spitting distance of the record.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼らは記録まで、あと一歩に迫りました。
nuance: Informal, almost always in within spitting distance of, with no article.
nuanceJapanese: ほぼつねに within spitting distance of の形で使い、冠詞は付けないくだけた表現。

meaning: Ruin others' enjoyment or success.
japanese: 場の喜びに、水を差す。
cue: Someone raises a problem during a celebration.
reply: I don't want to spoil the party, but the last train is at eleven.
replyJapanese: 水を差すようですが、終電は11時です。
transferReply: The visiting team spoiled the party.
transferReplyJapanese: 遠征チームが、祝賀に水を差しました。
nuance: Party takes the. It covers a real celebration and any moment of shared success.
nuanceJapanese: party には the を付ける。実際の祝いにも、成功の場面全般にも使う。

meaning: Try to do something that cannot be done.
japanese: 両立しないことを、やろうとする。
cue: Two requirements contradict each other.
reply: Cheaper and faster is squaring the circle.
replyJapanese: 安くて速くというのは、両立しません。
transferReply: The plan tries to square the circle.
transferReplyJapanese: その計画は、両立しないものを両立させようとしています。
nuance: Circle takes the. From an impossible geometry problem, so it implies the task cannot succeed.
nuanceJapanese: circle には the を付ける。解けない幾何学の問題に由来し、成立し得ないことを含意する。

meaning: Follow a chosen path between difficulties.
japanese: 難所のあいだを、舵取りして進む。
cue: A leader balances competing demands.
reply: She steers a course between the two demands.
replyJapanese: 彼女は2つの要求のあいだを、舵取りしています。
transferReply: The board steered a course through a difficult year.
transferReplyJapanese: 理事会は、難しい一年を舵取りしていきました。
frame: Steer a course between two things
nuance: Course takes a. An adjective can sit between them: steer a middle course.
nuanceJapanese: course には a を付ける。あいだに形容詞を挟むこともできる：steer a middle course。

meaning: Give an opinion where it is not wanted.
japanese: 頼まれもせず、口を挟む。
cue: Someone interrupts a private discussion.
reply: He had to stick his oar in, of course.
replyJapanese: 案の定、彼が口を挟んできました。
transferReply: Sorry to stick my oar in, but there's a typo.
transferReplyJapanese: 口を挟んですみませんが、誤字があります。
nuance: British and informal. The possessive follows the speaker. Stick is irregular: stuck.
nuanceJapanese: くだけたイギリス英語。所有格は口を挟む人に合わせる。stick は不規則変化で stuck。

meaning: Have a strong and immediate effect on someone.
japanese: 胸に、ずしりと届く。
cue: A remark affected someone deeply.
reply: That comment really struck home.
replyJapanese: あの一言は、深く刺さりました。
transferReply: The final example struck home with everyone.
transferReplyJapanese: 最後の例は、全員の胸に届きました。
nuance: Strike is irregular: struck. Home takes no article and works as an adverb here.
nuanceJapanese: strike は不規則変化で struck。home に冠詞は付かず、ここでは副詞として働く。

meaning: Win everything that was available.
japanese: ひとり勝ちで、総なめにする。
cue: One entrant won every category.
reply: Their film swept the board this year.
replyJapanese: 今年は、彼らの映画が賞を総なめにしました。
transferReply: The school swept the board at the championships.
transferReplyJapanese: その学校は、大会で総なめにしました。
nuance: British; American English says sweep the awards. Sweep is irregular: swept.
nuanceJapanese: イギリス英語で、アメリカ英語では sweep the awards と言う。sweep は不規則変化で swept。

meaning: Believe exactly what someone says.
japanese: 言葉どおりに、受け取る。
cue: A promise is accepted without proof.
reply: I took her at her word and booked it.
replyJapanese: 彼女の言葉を信じて、予約しました。
transferReply: We take people at their word here.
transferReplyJapanese: ここでは、人の言葉をそのまま信じます。
nuance: The possessive matches the person believed. Take is irregular: took, taken.
nuanceJapanese: 所有格は信じる相手に合わせる。take は不規則変化で took、taken。

meaning: Review a situation carefully before deciding.
japanese: 状況を見直して、整理する。
cue: A pause is needed after a busy period.
reply: Let's take stock of where we are.
replyJapanese: 今どこにいるのか、いったん整理しましょう。
transferReply: December is a good time to take stock of things.
transferReplyJapanese: 12月は、状況を見直すのによい時期です。
nuance: Stock takes no article. From counting goods in a shop, so it implies an honest inventory.
nuanceJapanese: stock に冠詞は付かない。店の棚卸しに由来し、率直な点検を含意する。

meaning: Do something without asking first, politely acknowledged.
japanese: 勝手ながら、先に済ませておく。
cue: You did something helpful without checking.
reply: I took the liberty of booking a room.
replyJapanese: 勝手ながら、部屋を押さえておきました。
transferReply: She took the liberty of correcting the date.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は勝手ながら、日付を直しておきました。
frame: Take the liberty of doing something
nuance: Liberty takes the, and of is followed by an -ing form. Polite and slightly formal.
nuanceJapanese: liberty には the を付け、of のあとは -ing 形。丁寧でやや改まった表現。

phrase: that's the way the cookie crumbles
meaning: Said to accept a disappointing result calmly.
japanese: 仕方がない、と受け入れる言い方。
cue: A bid was unsuccessful.
reply: We didn't get it, but that's the way the cookie crumbles.
replyJapanese: 取れませんでしたが、そういうものです。
transferReply: No refund, and that's the way the cookie crumbles.
transferReplyJapanese: 返金はなしです。まあ、そういうものです。
slug: that's the way the cookie crumbles
frame: That's the way the cookie crumbles
nuance: American, fixed and light in tone. It accepts the outcome rather than explaining it.
nuanceJapanese: アメリカ英語の、軽い調子の固定表現。説明ではなく、結果を受け入れる言い方。

phrase: the apple doesn't fall far from the tree
meaning: Children resemble their parents.
japanese: 子は親に似るものだ。
cue: A child shows a parent's habit.
reply: She argues just like her father — the apple doesn't fall far from the tree.
replyJapanese: お父さんそっくりの議論の仕方です。子は親に似ますね。
transferReply: He became a baker too, so the apple doesn't fall far from the tree.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼もパン職人になりました。やはり子は親に似ます。
slug: the apple doesn't fall far from the tree
frame: The apple doesn't fall far from the tree
nuance: Fixed. It can be warm or slightly critical, depending on the trait being described.
nuanceJapanese: 形は固定。どの性質を指すかで、温かくも、やや批判的にもなる。

meaning: The highest social class.
japanese: 社会の、いちばん上の層。
cue: Describe an exclusive club.
reply: The club was strictly the upper crust.
replyJapanese: そのクラブは、上流階級だけのものでした。
transferReply: It follows the upper crust of the 1920s.
transferReplyJapanese: それは1920年代の上流社会を描いています。
nuance: Always with the. Slightly humorous or distancing, so it is rarely used about oneself.
nuanceJapanese: つねに the を伴う。やや揶揄や距離感を含むため、自分については使いにくい。

meaning: Increase pressure on someone to act.
japanese: 圧力を強めて、締め上げる。
cue: A buyer pressed a supplier harder.
reply: They tightened the screws on late payers.
replyJapanese: 彼らは支払いの遅い相手に、圧力を強めました。
transferReply: The rules tighten the screws on landlords.
transferReplyJapanese: その規則は、家主への締めつけを強めます。
nuance: Screws is always plural with the. On introduces who is being pressed.
nuanceJapanese: screws は the を伴う複数形。圧力を受ける側は on で示す。

meaning: Make brief contact to exchange news.
japanese: 手短に、近況を確認し合う。
cue: You want a quick update from a colleague.
reply: I'll touch base with you on Thursday.
replyJapanese: 木曜に、少し状況を確認させてください。
transferReply: We touch base with the team every month.
transferReplyJapanese: 毎月、チームと連絡を取り合っています。
nuance: From baseball. Base is singular with no article, and with introduces the person.
nuanceJapanese: 野球由来。base は冠詞なしの単数形で、相手は with で示す。

meaning: Run away from something suddenly.
japanese: きびすを返して、逃げ出す。
cue: Someone left as soon as trouble appeared.
reply: They turned tail at the first sign of trouble.
replyJapanese: 彼らは面倒の気配を察して、すぐ逃げ出しました。
transferReply: The fox turned tail and disappeared.
transferReplyJapanese: きつねはきびすを返して、消えました。
nuance: Tail takes no article. Often followed by and run or and flee, and it implies cowardice.
nuanceJapanese: tail に冠詞は付かない。and run や and flee を続けることが多く、臆病さを含意する。

meaning: Good for everyone involved.
japanese: 双方にとって、得になる。
cue: An arrangement suits both sides.
reply: Sharing the space is win-win.
replyJapanese: 場所を分け合うのは、双方に得です。
transferReply: It was a win-win outcome for both firms.
transferReplyJapanese: 両社にとって、得になる結果でした。
nuance: Hyphenated and used as an adjective. Common in business writing, and always positive.
nuanceJapanese: ハイフンで結び、形容詞として使う。ビジネス文書でよく使い、つねに肯定的。

meaning: Repeated exactly, without a single mistake.
japanese: 一語も違えず、完璧に。
cue: Someone delivered a speech from memory.
reply: She was word perfect throughout.
replyJapanese: 彼女は最後まで、一語も違えませんでした。
transferReply: The cast was word perfect by Friday.
transferReplyJapanese: 金曜までに、出演者は台詞を完璧にしていました。
nuance: British; American English says word for word. Often hyphenated before a noun.
nuanceJapanese: イギリス英語で、アメリカ英語では word for word と言う。名詞の前ではハイフンを付けることが多い。
